<STRUCT_0001>
A V covering gives a universally submersive family of maps.
The converse of this lemma is false, see
Examples, Section <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a V covering.
Then
<MATH_0002>
is a universally submersive morphism of schemes (Morphisms, Definition
<REF_0001>).

We will use without further mention that the base change of a V covering
is a V covering (Lemma <REF_0001>). In particular it suffices
to show that the morphism is submersive.
Being submersive is clearly Zariski local on the base.
Thus we may assume <MATH_0001> is affine. Then <MATH_0002>
can be refined by a standard V covering <MATH_0003>.
If we can show that <MATH_0004> is submersive,
then since there is a factorization <MATH_0005>
we conclude that <MATH_0006> is submersive.
Set <MATH_0007> and consider the morphism of affines
<MATH_0008>.
By Lemma <REF_0002> we know that we can lift any
specialization <MATH_0009> in <MATH_0010> to some specialization
<MATH_0011> in <MATH_0012>.
Thus if <MATH_0013> is a subset such that <MATH_0014>
is closed in <MATH_0015>, then <MATH_0016> is closed under specialization.
Since <MATH_0017>
with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure
is an affine scheme, we conclude that <MATH_0018> is closed by
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence <MATH_0019> is submersive.
